summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book (Book 14, part 84), the narrator arranges to stay overnight at a friend's lake cottage in Sibley County, deliberately dropping hints to Monica that the trip may be risky while assuring her it will be safe. Monica reluctantly agrees and they say I love you. Nikko, unable to reach his parents, proposes borrowing a car from Bree, a purple-haired girl who was active in the protest over arrests, and the two argue about whether Bree should be involved and whether the Solidarity Committee is sincere.
one_line: The narrator plans a risky trip to Sibley County and argues with Nikko over borrowing Bree's car after a protest over arrests.
key_facts: The narrator is set to stay overnight with a friend from school whose family has a lake cottage in Sibley County.
The friend says there is a wood stove, that she and the narrator will not party, and that the friend's dog is a good watchdog.
The narrator chose Sibley County deliberately because both characters thought there were too many monuments and places named after Henry Hastings Sibley.
The narrator worries that someone from the Joint Terrorism Task Force could be listening in on the phone call.
Monica says "Take care of yourself" and "I love you" before the call ends, and the narrator replies "Love you, too."
Nikko tries to reach his parents twice and hangs up both times without leaving messages.
Nikko's dad is in court that day, and his mom is out of town on a business trip.
Nikko proposes borrowing a car from a friend he describes as someone he would trust with his life.
The narrator identifies the friend with the car as the purple-haired girl, whose name is Bree.
The narrator says Bree would be putting herself at risk and asks whether Nikko is sure he wants that.
Bree was at the protest tabling for the Solidarity Committee, according to Nikko.
The narrator dismisses the Solidarity Committee as people who want to get on television.
Nikko says the narrator is not being very rational, which the narrator resents.
Nikko quickly apologizes and backpedals after the narrator's reaction.
